title: Derived transposition on a tensor model with one K-flat factor
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and use module complexes and localization $Q$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $P$ be a K-flat complex with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex], $E$ a K-injective complex [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $A$ any unbounded complex. Use the total tensor, product Hom complex and normalized derived tensor-Hom structure [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] [def-pur-hom-complex] [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Then $Q(A\otimes_R P)$ canonically computes $QA\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QP$. For every chain map $f:A\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,E)$, its derived tensor-Hom transpose is represented by $\widetilde f:A\otimes_R P\to E$, $a\otimes p\mapsto f(a)(p)$. These comparisons are natural in $A,P,E$ and agree with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms of representatives; no K-flatness of $A$ or boundedness is required. The order of factors is $A,P$; interchanging homogeneous factors of degrees $n,m$ introduces $(-1)^{nm}$.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (sites-cohomology-lemma-internal-hom), proof: arbitrary first complex and K-flat second factor; agent refinement fixing the chain transpose on one-sided models.

proof.text: For fixed P, use the existing K-flat tensor quasi-isomorphism theorem to show that H(A)=Q(Tot(A,P)) inverts quasi-isomorphisms. The inclusion of all K-flat complexes followed by Q is a localization, as proved by the K-flat localization helper of the existing tensor-Hom adjunction module. Lift H along Q, and lift the fixed natural two-K-flat comparison through the fully faithful whiskering functor. Composing with the localization factorization gives a natural isomorphism H≅S.tensor(Q(-),QP). Its restriction equals the given T.iso because map_preimage cancels the factorization and its inverse.

Naturality in A is the naturality of this isomorphism. To prove naturality in a map b:P→P′, choose a K-flat resolution q:F→A. The total tensor square commutes by functoriality. At F the desired equation is naturality of T.comparison. Apply first-variable naturality on its two sides, and cancel the invertible image of q tensor id_P. This does not require flatness or boundedness of A.

Use the already proved chainEquiv of the ringed derived tensor-Hom adjunction module. Its inverse constructs the ordinary chain uncurrying map for arbitrary complexes, with its proved unsigned pure-section formula and its simultaneous chain naturality. The existing complexConstraints theorem gives the actual Koszul sign on factor interchange.

For K-flat A, apply the existing coefficientTensorCurry_normalize theorem to chainEquiv inverse and its pure-section formula. Multiply by T.iso.hom and cancel T.iso.inv. This proves exactly the fixed transpose equation, before any resolution of A.

For arbitrary A choose a K-flat resolution q:F→A. First-variable naturality of the comparison, left naturality of the given adjunction Hom equivalence, and chain uncurrying naturality identify the two sides after precomposition by Q(q tensor id_P). Apply the preceding K-flat equation at F and cancel this invertible map. The augmentation in this formula is definitionally the same fixed K-injective augmentation as in the normalization theorem.

For quasi-isomorphisms in both tensor representatives, comparison naturality expresses the localized tensor map as conjugate to S.tensor applied to two localized isomorphisms; hence it is invertible. The independent-universe Hom quasi-isomorphism theorem gives Hom representative inversion. Apply it also to the identity of P and the fixed augmentation E→I(E), whose source and target are K-injective, to prove that the Hom comparison is invertible. Assemble these results in the original eleven-field structure.
